group.passage: Native to the Pacific and Indian oceans, lionfish are now established in the western Atlantic Ocean, the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea, where they have very few predators and have become a damaging threat to the well-being of coral reefs and other marine ecosystems. Lionfish are carnivores, eating small crustaceans and fish with a voracious appetite. In just five weeks, a single lionfish can reduce the number of young fish in its feeding zone by 80 percent, including important commercial fish species such as snappers and groupers. Furthermore, their reproductive output is extraordinary with females able to lay around 25,000 eggs a day. As lionfish populations grow, they put additional stress on coral reefs. For example, lionfish eat the cleaner fish which helps maintain algae at a level that will allow enough sunlight in for the coral reefs to, in turn, produce most of the world’s oxygen. If lionfish remain unchecked, coral reef extinction is a sure outcome and will dramatically alter the environment and economy for the worse. A number of strategies have been used to stem lionfish populations. On Bonaire, a Dutch island in the Caribbean Sea, actions rely on volunteer lionfish hunters. As spearfishing is prohibited on Bonaire, special tools called ELF (eradicate lionfish) have been developed to assist divers in their hunts. These tools also help prevent damage caused by traditional spear guns and nets on reefs. An additional tool called “zookeeper,” a piece of PVC pipe with a modified plastic funnel at one end and sealed at the other, is used to help remove the fish from the spear tip of an ELF without being injured by their poisonous spines. The lionfish is inserted into the zookeeper once it is speared on the ELF. When the spear is withdrawn, the fish is trapped inside the pipe by the funnel. Although killing lionfish may be seen as cruel, it is currently the most practical way to slow the destruction they are causing to the reefs.

options.B: Lionfish’s spines release poisonous chemicals which pollute the ocean.
options.C: Lack of predators is the main cause of lionfish’s growing population.
options.D: Cleaner fish can produce a large quantity of oxygen in their habitats.
